My uncle always had a large garden. When I say large I mean 1 acre or so. He pretty much kept the whole extended family in fresh veggies during the gardening season. When he got older and couldn't do the work it takes to have a large garden he sold his place and bought a much smaller home with a small front and back lawn. But he never lost the love to garden so he started gardening small. One of the things that impressed me the most was how he grew potatoes in old car tires. He would fill the inside of a tire with soil and plant a few potato plants. Once the plants grew to a few inches tall he would pack dirt and mulch around them which encouraged them to grow taller. Once they reached a certain height he would stack another tire on top of the first one and keep building the stack of tires. When he harvested the potatoes he simply started by taking the top tire off. Potatoes would line the inside of the tire where the "air" or tube would go on a working tire. I've seen him stack them 4 tires high with every tire loaded with potatoes. This was some years back, my uncle is deceased now.
